name: Ilyas (Elijah)
source: Stories of the Prophets — compiled from the Qur'an and authentic hadith
paras: "And indeed, Ilyas was from among the messengers." (As-Saffat 37:123) — Ilyas was sent to the kingdom of Israel after the twelve tribes divided, in the generations after Sulaiman, when the worship of the idol Ba'l had spread in the land.

He stood almost alone against a court and a populace given to idolatry: "O my people, do you not fear Allah? Do you call upon Ba'l and leave the best of creators — Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your first fathers?" (As-Saffat 37:124-126).

His challenge was the creed of tauhid in a single sentence: your Lord is not the idol of the groves but the Creator of your fathers themselves — the Best of creators, before whom Ba'l is a carved block.

The people rejected him, and the Qur'an records their end: "So they will be brought forth to the punishment, and they will be a people reproached" (As-Saffat 37:127) — except the sincere believers whom Allah kept for Himself.

In the earlier scriptures his name is Elijah the Tishbite, the prophet of Mount Carmel whose contest with the prophets of Ba'l ended in the people's cry, "The Lord, He is God!" — a history that circles the same Qur'anic centre: one prophet against a kingdom of idols.
The Qur'an crowns him among the righteous: "Peace be upon Ilyas. Thus do We reward the doers of good. Indeed, he was of Our believing servants." (As-Saffat 37:129-132).
Ilyas remains the emblem of the lone caller: one voice against a nation, sustained not by numbers but by the Lord of the first fathers and the last.
